title: Deployment grease logs and runbook edits (Mar 2026)
body:
Purpose
This doc captures the week-of Mar 16–22, 2026 grease-log entries from on-prem/VPC installs, small runbook edits we validated, and action items for reducing repeated friction during customer handoffs. Not a formal postmortem — quick operational notes and where we’ll edit the runbook.

Attendees
Avery Chen (owner), Diego Morales, Priya Nair, Samir Patel, Kelsea Romero, oncall: Maria Liu (SRE)

High-level summary (TL;DR)
- Three installs progressed to day-two; two had transient infra issues that caused longer handoffs.
- Recurring friction: network egress/firewall rules, NTP drift on appliances, and KMS/HSM token rotation misunderstandings.
- We patched the runbook in-place with three small edits (port checklist, NTP verification step, KMS sanity check) and validated them on a staging install.

Grease log entries (operational timeline)
Mar 17 09:12 — Customer: AtlasFin (onprem, rack install)
- Symptom: Control-plane agents repeatedly failing to retrieve KMS keys after token rotation. Error: 401 from customer HSM gateway.
- Investigation: Customer rotated tokens on their HSM without notifying us; their gateway IP changed (NAT). The installer’s KMS endpoint config used hostname only; DNS TTL still pointed to old nat.
- Workaround: Added temporary hosts entry on installer node, regenerated short-lived token, restarted control-plane.
- Runbook action: Add explicit KMS hostname+IP verification and 'validate KMS endpoint after rotation' checklist (see runbook section below).

Mar 18 14:45 — Customer: CartoHealth (VPC)
- Symptom: High tail latency for first 30s of traffic post-deploy; CPU spike on model-serving nodes.
- Investigation: KV cache cold-start plus simultaneous integration test traffic from CI. Batching scheduler pushed long tail.
- Workaround: Warm KV cache with small synthetic load and gate CI traffic until health-checks green. Also bumped autoscale policy to allow small initial burst for 10 min.
- Runbook action: Add 'KV warmup' checklist and recommendation for gating external traffic.

Mar 20 02:05 — Customer: Redwood Retail (onprem)
- Symptom: Night-shift oncall noticed intermittent BMC (iLO) timeouts while we were trying to remote to a bad node.
- Investigation: Rack PDU had flaky power path B; node had NTP drift and cert expiry warnings. Remote console wouldn't open intermittently.
- Workaround: Site tech cycled PDU on that PDU leg; node came back, we rotated certs locally.
- Runbook action: Add note to confirm rack PDU health and NTP sync before remote console ops.

Runbook edits applied (validated on staging)
1) Quick network checklist (new step inserted after "preflight ports"): confirm both CIDR and NAT public egress IPs listed by customer, and recommend an explicit mapping table for NAT translations (why: DNS+NAT changes caused KMS failures).
2) NTP & cert sanity (new step): verify NTP sources, check cert expiry (openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -dates), and if drift > 5s, perform NTP correction and retest services.
3) KMS rotation sanity (new step): after any key rotation, run: curl --resolve <kms-host>:443:<expected-ip> https://<kms-host>/health and verify token retrieval locally.
4) Warmup guidance (appendix): short sequence for KV cache warmup, recommended synthetic traffic pattern (50 small requests over 30s) and gating CI.

Open blockers and risks (with owners & expected dates)
- PD-2110 (KMS rotation playbook gaps) — Owner: Diego Morales — ETA for full playbook rewrite: 2026-04-02. Reason: current runbook only documents first-time install flow.
- ENG-6189 (KV warmup automation) — Owner: Priya Nair — ETA for simple script + helm hook: 2026-03-30. Risk: until automated, human gating is inconsistent.
- Networking: some enterprise customers want shared egress IPs whitelisted for multi-region failover — Owner: Samir Patel — PR open to installer: #472 — target merge: 2026-03-26.

Decisions made in meeting
- Short-term: adopt runbook edits above immediately (done on staging). Communicate to field via a short Slack broadcast and update the Confluence preflight page.
- Medium-term: standardize a small 'preflight artifact' customers supply (CSV: NAT mappings, egress IPs, NTP servers, BMC ranges). Engineering to own schema; SEs to adopt during kickoff.

Action items (concrete)
- Diego: Draft KMS rotation playbook section and share by 2026-03-26 (linked to PD-2110).
- Priya: Implement KV warmup helm hook + script; initial PR by 2026-03-26, merge by 2026-03-30.
- Samir: Finish PR #472 to accept egress-ip list and add validation errors; target 2026-03-26.
- Avery: Publish a 1-page "day-zero checklist" (customer-facing) and post to Confluence by 2026-03-24.
- Kelsea: Create a small field-training slide (5 slides) for install techs covering NTP and PDU checks; due 2026-03-29.

Lessons learned / patterns
- The majority of friction this week stemmed from infrastructure changes on the customer side that aren’t fully captured in our preflight intake. A light-weight artifact from customers (see "Decision") will reduce these interrupts.
- Cold KV cache + simultaneous CI traffic is a recurring source of bad first impressions. We should socialize warmup patterns with growth/SEs.

Quick checklist for next installs (copyable)
- [ ] Confirm egress IPs + NAT mapping CSV present
- [ ] Validate NTP servers respond and drift < 5s
- [ ] Check rack PDU reported alarms in BMC (if onprem)
- [ ] Validate KMS endpoint by IP and hostname after any rotation
- [ ] Gate CI/integration traffic until KV warmup script runs

Notes / references
- Confluence preflight: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=9876543
- Related JIRA: PD-2110, ENG-6189
- Installer PR (egress ip validation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/installer/pull/472
- Slack thread (ops): #onprem-install-thread/archives/CB12AB34

If anything missing or you want me to open separate tickets for the runbook language changes, call it out in-thread — will push the Confluence update after PRs merge.

-- Avery
